newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates higher, offer scarce.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates higher, offer scarce.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates remained higher in Tuesday morning trade amid shortage of kuna funds, dealers said.
"There is no money and demand for kuna is enormously high. Banks simply take everything that is on offer," one dealer said.
She said the banks' deposits had shrunk over the past few days and hinted a central bank intervention may well be needed.
Call money loans accounted for most of 20.5 million kuna fresh borrowings made by mid-morning.
The shortage kept the call money rate higher at 11 percent like Monday, but up 50 basis points from last week.
Other interbank rates ranged between 15 and 18 percent, depending on term.

Overnight trade on Monday totalled 43 million kuna, of which 3.8 million were granted to two banks with shortfalls. The rest went for maintenance of statutory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
